show: My Favorite Murder with Karen Kilgariff and Georgia Hardstark

einzeiler: The unsolved 1987 murder of Sherry Orofino and the chaotic 1928 transcontinental foot…
kurzfassung: The hosts discuss the 1987 murder of Sherry Orofino in New York, focusing on a police officer who was investigated after several women reported being harassed on the same highway. They also explore the 1928 Bunyan Derby, a grueling, poorly organized foot race across America created by sports agent C.C. Pyle. The episode blends true crime investigation with historical endurance sports storytelling.
stichpunkte: Sherry Orofino disappeared in February 1987 while driving from Queens to her new home in Millbrook, New York.
Her sports car was found locked and abandoned near the Taconic State Parkway, and her remains were discovered months later.
Multiple women reported being stopped and harassed along the same stretch of road by a local police officer named Ronald Langer.
Langer was eventually convicted on federal civil rights charges for pulling over and harassing women, but was never tried for the murder.
The hosts shift to the centenary of Route 66 and the 1928 transcontinental foot race known as the Bunyan Derby.
Promoted by sports agent C.C. Pyle, nearly 200 men set out to run over 3,400 miles from Los Angeles to New York City.
Runners faced extreme conditions, lack of proper footwear, terrible sleeping arrangements, and danger from active roadways.
Oklahoma farm boy Andy Payne ultimately won the grueling race after nearly three months on the road.

clips.hook: A police officer pulling over women on the highway
clips.text: Several witnesses reported that a law enforcement official had pulled over a blonde driver in the exact area where the victim's vehicle was later discovered.

clips.hook: A massive cash prize for an ocean swim
clips.text: Participants in a grueling 1927 California coastal swimming event competed for a reward worth half a million dollars today.
A participant who sang while running quenched his thirst from a gas station bucket, failing to realize it contained fuel instead of water.
